Visual identity, website and curation for Offener Kanal Europa, a media platform and collective that began in 2020 as a TV channel in a former snack kiosk in Berlin’s Europacity, and that has since documented, through interviews and artistic actions, how urban privatisation reshapes the city.

Offener Kanal Europa is a media platform and series of interventions in public space, initiated by Nora Spiekermann in collaboration with Giacomo Marinsalta and active in Berlin since 2020. Through interviews and street-level artistic and community-led actions, it documents how the financialisation of urban space, especially the privatisation of real estate, is transforming the city.

The project began in summer 2020, when Offener Kanal Europa took over a former Imbiss (snack kiosk) in Europacity, a privately developed neighbourhood in Berlin. The birdhouse-shaped kiosk became the studio of a mobile TV channel and hosted a range of events. The first series of interviews asked: What moves Europacity? What should the neighbourhood look like in the future? How is public space changing? Watch the first TV channel of Europacity, Berlin, here.


Die Stadt als Papier denken

Performance in public space

In August 2021, to celebrate the publication of the fanzine Lothars letzte Reise, Offener Kanal Europa organised Die Stadt als Papier denken, a performance in public space. At a mobile DIY station, passers-by in the streets of Europacity cut and folded the zines themselves.

Lothars letzte Reise tells the story of an elderly resident of Wedding visiting the Europacity district for the first time. Contrasts emerge between what the city used to be and what it is becoming. The fanzine was published by ZNAAACKS Publications.

Cheerful Weaves: Laboratory for Joyful Dependencies
A documentary film on a week-long residency that experimented with collective practices of care, taking place at Libken, in Gerswalde, Germany in 2021.

Growing out of conversations and reflections shared since spring 2020, Cheerful Weaves – Labor für gelungene Abhängigkeiten (tr. Laboratory for Joyful Dependencies) was a self-organised process for reflecting on and experimenting with collective practices of care.
As the pandemic unfolded, close exchanges between friends awakened a joyful, militant wish to explore the mutual responsibilities and needs we share in caring for, with, of and about each other, while holding a critical stance towards the structures of power and domination that shape society.

Cheerful Weaves took place at Libken e.V. from 12 to 19 September 2021, with a week-long residency for invited artists Olga Golde, Ronald Berger, Giulia Claudia Massacci, Marina Prados, Paula Knüpling and Kaitlin Fisher.

In collaboration with Libken e.V., Paula Becker, Louis Mauff and Kim Sanou.
Funded by the Kulturstiftung des Bundes.
Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis
A video installation that reads Expo 2020 Dubai through Plato’s myth of Atlantis.

Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis is a video installation built around an experimental film on Expo 2020 Dubai, the world exposition held in 2021–2022.

The film draws on Plato’s myth of Atlantis, the island empire that sank beneath the sea at the height of its civilisation and power. The installation translates the mythical imagery of Atlantis into the aesthetics of Dubai’s free trade zones, luxury real estate and Expo sightseeing, as symbols of new social orders and new frontiers of cosmopolitan urbanism. Combining commercials with personal travel footage of a journey through the city to the Expo site, the work examines how the Expo represents the world – a form of “worlding” – blurring the line between reality and fiction.

Atlantis becomes a legendary tourist destination, reflecting a Western tendency to romanticise and exoticise faraway places, and an othering, voyeuristic gaze drawn to the promise of an unknown elsewhere. The narrative unfolds within a surveilled, enclosed and temporary fair where political expression is pushed to the margins. Passports become branded souvenirs, symbols of a manufactured global encounter that suggests everyone shares the same freedom of movement.

Immersive experiences, idealistic rhetoric on sustainability and promises of “real-world” solutions stage a worldly narrative that enchants virtual visitors and passing spectators alike. Whether imagined as a utopian “island of the blessed”, an oasis in the desert or a distant land on the horizon, Atlantis remains a mirage: an elusive vision of progress woven with nationalist dreams and an incessant stream of virtual landscapes, whose “concrete” realisation is forever being improved and perfected.

Video and installation by Giacomo Marinsalta
Music by Aïna Spencer

The installation was exhibited at the conference Un/Reale Interaktionsräume at FH Potsdam in November 2022, funded by the ZEM programme “Digital Realities”. An essay on the work appears in the publication of the same name, Un/Reale Interaktionsräume (transcript Verlag, 2025).

A six-episode street interview series and a live performance on life around Alexanderplatz, made with Nora Spiekermann for the Haus der Statistik in Berlin as part of the collective Offener Kanal Europa.

In 2022, the Offener Kanal Europa collective explored the neighbourhood around Alexanderplatz as part of the open call gemeinsam um die Häuser ziehen, launched by the Haus der Statistik.

Nora Spiekermann and Giacomo Marinsalta asked passers-by: What is it like to live right on Alexanderplatz? Do people know about the Haus der Statistik? What value does the project hold for the city centre?

Their research led to a large live broadcast on the street in front of the Haus der Statistik, a six-episode interview series titled Alles Anders TV, and two performative tours of the neighbourhood. Alles Anders TV was broadcast by the TV station and media platform ALEX Berlin.

Wicked Games – For a Morphology of Gestures is a series of visual artworks on the body’s spasmodic response to digitisation, published in Queerpandemia: Contaminazioni Artistiche di Altro Genere (Tlon & TWM Factory, 2024).

Wicked Games – For a Morphology of Gestures is a series of scanographies in which movement appears as the body’s spasmodic response to the pervasiveness of digitisation. Hands move erratically in response to the machine’s glitched impressions. Skin merges with stone as an outgrowth of the world. Its textures interweave with objects and their appearances in the rhythm of a shared becoming.

During the pandemic, the invisible agency of the virus heightened a fear closely bound to the body, while media and news kept the possibility of death constantly in view. Behind the gestures, a cosmic void stands for the sense of meaninglessness that many of us felt at the time.

As images lost their meaning through constant consumption in an endless virtual flow, the series turned to the physical qualities of the mineral world, whose slow crystalline transformations remain imperceptible to the human eye. Over millennia, minute changes in terrestrial conditions shape minerals into evocative forms and signs. A key reference for the series is Roger Caillois’s The Writing of Stones (L’Écriture des pierres, 1970), which reads the patterns found in stones as a kind of writing produced by nature itself.

Featured in Queerpandemia – Contaminazioni artistiche di altro genere (Tlon, 2023).

Curation and illustrations for a climate change horoscope app project reading our future in climate science rather than the stars. The research resulted in an illustrated horoscope, published in the Zeitschrift für Medienwissenschaft (transcript Verlag, 2024).

Drawing on astrology and grounded in climate science, Climate Fortunes is a web app offering a glimpse into a future that is more certain than we might wish.

The project was developed during the Environmental Data, Media and the Humanities Hackathon, held in Potsdam from 31 May to 2 June 2023 and organised by the Network of Digital Humanities at the University of Potsdam. It was created by Lukas Diestel, Maximilian Hepach, Giacomo Marinsalta, Sybille Neumeyer, Jonas Parnow, Birgit Schneider and May Ee Wong, with funding from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation. The source code is available on GitHub.

The research has also led to the article “Horoskop”, illustrated by Giacomo Marinsalta and published in the Zeitschrift für Medienwissenschaft (2024).

A video poem and installation following sheets and clothes hung out to dry in a Mediterranean city, where laundry blurs the line between public and private and becomes a sign of care and resistance.

Video poem and installation by Giacomo Marinsalta
Music by Lola Lextrait

Can an everyday gesture and an ordinary object such as laundry, usually excluded from the aesthetic gaze, reveal a beauty of their own?
The words of a poem accompany a life suspended between dream and reality, on a journey through sheets and clothes hanging in the wind along the streets of a Mediterranean city. Laundry blurs the boundaries between inside and outside, public and private. Across narrow alleys, balconies and windows, fabric becomes language, architectural ornament and a symbol of care and resistance, in contrast with urban policies increasingly governed by an aesthetics of decorum.

The project grew out of the research for a Master of Arts thesis in European Media Studies at the University of Potsdam, “Laundering Dreams in the Porous City: The Political Aesthetics of Laundry in Public Space”.

An interactive walk by the collective Offener Kanal Europa through the hidden green spaces of Europacity, a privatised district of Berlin.

The Offener Kanal Europa collective, founded by Nora Spiekermann and Giacomo Marinsalta, invited participants to discover the hidden green spaces of Europacity, a fast-developing privatised district of Berlin. Amid the spreading concrete, the walk examined the shifting boundaries between public and private space, and between genuine sustainability and greenwashing.
